description.narrative:
The Dutch SRHR Alliance is a two-and-a-half-year pilot partnership (2026–2028) bringing together 11 organizations committed to advancing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), resilient health systems, and inclusive youth participation across multiple countries.
The Alliance seeks to protect and strengthen SRHR in a global context characterized by shrinking development funding, increasing anti-rights movements, and weakened health systems. Together with implementing partners in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Mali, Niger, and Uganda, the Alliance responds to the urgent need for sustained investment in SRHR and stronger, more resilient health systems. Investing in fair play is both a commitment to human rights and a strategicapproach to achieving sustainable social impact.
All 11 members of the Dutch SRHR Alliance contribute significant value to the partnership through governance, programme implementation, learning, and knowledge exchange. Key organizations including Amref, Oxfam Novib, and Wemos provide centralmanagement roles, while Hivos, Rutgers, Liliane Fonds, Amref, and Plan International support country-level coordination and mentorship. Choice plays a leading role in strengthening Meaningful and Inclusive Youth Participation across the Alliance’s governance structures.
In addition, organizations such as CoC, VSO, and Aidsfonds contribute technical expertise through participation in knowledge exchange meetings, learning sessions, and collaborative activities coordinated by the Alliance Hub. The partnership emphasizes shared learning, innovation, and cross-country collaboration to strengthenprogramme effectiveness and long-term sustainability. At the global level, the Alliance operates through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), while governance modalities will be further refinedduring the inception phase. Currently, the Directors’ Meeting—comprising representatives from all 11 organizations—serves as the principal decision-making body for global planning andbudgeting. Decisions are made through consensus whenever possible, or by a two-thirds majority vote when required.

participating-org.narrative: Within the Uniersal Access to Female Condoms (UAFC) Joint Programme, Rutgers WPF is responsible for advocacy, linking and leariningand communication componet. The Dutch World Population Foundation (WPF) was founded in 1987. Its main goal then was to push back high birth rates and high rates of maternal and infant mortality, thus to decrease world poverty. From 1987 to 1994 it remained a small organisation, mainly supported by donations from its founders and consultancy assignments. In 1994 the WPF played an important role in the Dutch delegation at the International Conference on Population and Development in Cairo, where the Cairo Program of Action was adopted, the focus of WPF's work ever since. WPF merged in 2011 with the Rutgers Foundation and became Rutgers WPF. It still focuses on self-determination, sexual health and reproductive rights, both in the Netherlands as well as in developing countries. It has became an expert organisation in the field of sexual and reproductive health and rights.
